description: Accepted differences for fidelity/run.js (see lib/accepted.js). DENY BY DEFAULT: a difference fails the gate unless its exact key appears here. Keys are PER DIFF, not per page, and are printed by the gate so an entry can be copied straight from its output — `fidelity:L1: {url} {-|+} "{text}"`, `fidelity:L2: {url} {field} golden={n} converted={n}`, `fidelity:L3: {url} {type} {path}#{anchor}`. Accepting one difference on a page leaves every other difference on it blocking. Each entry needs a `disposition` (wont-fix | upstream | harness-limit | deferred) and a non-empty `note`; a malformed entry fails the gate. Accepted differences are still PRINTED on every run and written to build/diff/fidelity-report.json. A STALE entry (its difference no longer occurs) FAILS the gate, so this cannot become a record of what used to be broken. A page-level `error` (no main-content container) is deliberately NOT acceptable: there is no diff to judge, so accepting it would mute the whole page. Prefer fixing a difference over accepting it, and reach for `harness-limit` only after checking the RENDERED output, since a comparator blind spot is a harness bug rather than a discrepancy (the admonition-title strip fixed on 2026-08-17 was one).

fidelity:L1: /operator/latest-snapshot/s.note: UPSTREAM SOURCE BUG in hazelcast-platform-operator-docs `docs/modules/ROOT/pages/scale.adoc`: a list continuation `+` is left dangling after a closed listing block, immediately before the block title `.For Openshift`. Asciidoctor therefore never reads that line as the next block's title and renders both lines as a literal paragraph — the LIVE docs site shows "+ .For Openshift" as stray text above the `oc apply` block today. Present on main, v/5.17 and v/5.18 (introduced after 5.16, which does not have the block). Our converter repairs it (fixSwallowedBlockTitles), so this diff is the golden's broken text that we deliberately do NOT reproduce. Fix = delete the stray `+` in the source; the entry then goes stale and the gate will say so.

The other half of the scale.adoc diff above: the block title `For Openshift` that our output HAS and the golden does not, because the golden left it as literal paragraph text. Not new content — the same words, correctly attached to the code block that follows.

fidelity:L1: /operator/5.18/image-regist.note: UPSTREAM SOURCE BUG in hazelcast-platform-operator-docs `docs/antora.yml` on the RELEASE branches: v/5.17 and v/5.18 both declare `snapshot: true`, which belongs only on main and was copied over when those branches were cut (v/5.16 is clean, which is exactly why 5.16 does not show this diff). image-registry.adoc wraps this note in `ifdef::snapshot[]`, so Antora renders it on those released versions — the LIVE 5.18 and 5.17 pages currently tell readers there are no Red Hat images for "snapshot versions". Fix = delete `snapshot: true` from v/5.17 and v/5.18 antora.yml; the entry then goes stale and the gate will say so.

fidelity:L2: /management-center/5.9/inte.note: prometheus-monitoring.adoc:216 — `` `http://localhost:2222/metrics` `` in backticks WITHOUT the `\` escape, so Asciidoctor linked it. The same URL on system-properties.adoc:892 IS escaped and renders correctly — the clearest evidence this is an authoring slip, not intent. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, accepted by Miranda 2026-08-18. The golden turns a PLACEHOLDER URL — an address the reader types or opens on their own machine, never a navigable destination — into a live link, because Asciidoctor autolinks a bare `http://…` (and does so even inside backticks unless the author writes `\http://…`). We render these as inline code with no link, which is what the 6 correctly authored occurrences elsewhere in the component already render as. Same judgement the Layer-2 `links` filter already records for an angle-bracket pseudo-URL (`http://<mc-ip-address>:8080`, where the converter drops the un-followable anchor and keeps the code), extended from "cannot be a valid URL" to "is not a real destination". The corpus authors this five different ways across MC, rendering three different ways; the converter normalises it. Layer 1 is unaffected — an inline <code> stays part of the prose text. UPSTREAM REPORT: the source should use `` `\http://…` ``. Fixing it there makes this entry go stale and the gate will say so.
